test_cases.description: Foundational programming concepts including variables, control flow, functions, and basic data structures. Emphasis on problem-solving and algorithmic thinking.
Introduction to web technologies: HTML, CSS, JavaScript. Building responsive websites and understanding client-server architecture.
Introduction to relational databases, SQL, data modeling, normalization, and basic database design principles.
Comprehensive study of fundamental data structures (arrays, linked lists, trees, graphs, hash tables) and algorithmic analysis. Emphasis on time/space complexity.
Advanced programming using OOP principles: encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, design patterns, and software architecture.
Server-side web development with RESTful APIs, authentication, database integration, and deployment. Covers Node.js, Express, and modern backend practices.
Comprehensive machine learning course covering supervised/unsupervised learning, neural networks, deep learning, model evaluation, and practical applications.
Advanced topics in distributed computing: consensus algorithms, fault tolerance, distributed databases, microservices, and scalability patterns.
Theory and practice of compiler construction: lexical analysis, parsing, semantic analysis, code generation, and optimization techniques.
Introduction to Python programming: syntax, data types, control structures, functions, modules, and file I/O. Practical coding exercises throughout.
Differential and integral calculus of functions of one variable. Limits, derivatives, applications, integration techniques, and fundamental theorem of calculus.
Vector spaces, matrices, linear transformations, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors. Applications to systems of linear equations and geometric transformations.
Descriptive statistics, probability distributions, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, and regression analysis. Emphasis on practical applications.
Rigorous treatment of real numbers, sequences, series, continuity, differentiation, and integration. Emphasis on proofs and theoretical foundations.
Group theory, ring theory, field theory. Study of algebraic structures and their properties with applications to number theory and cryptography.
Point-set topology, topological spaces, continuity, compactness, connectedness, and fundamental group. Introduction to algebraic topology.
Theory and applications of PDEs: wave equation, heat equation, Laplace equation. Solution methods including separation of variables and Fourier series.
Logic, sets, combinatorics, graph theory, and mathematical induction. Essential foundations for computer science.
Newtonian mechanics: kinematics, dynamics, work and energy, momentum, rotational motion, and gravitation. Laboratory component included.
Electric fields, magnetic fields, circuits, electromagnetic induction, and Maxwell's equations. Laboratory experiments with circuits and electromagnetic phenomena.
Introduction to quantum theory: wave-particle duality, Schrödinger equation, quantum operators, harmonic oscillator, and hydrogen atom.
Laws of thermodynamics, entropy, heat engines, phase transitions, and introduction to statistical mechanics. Connections to microscopic theory.
Standard model of particle physics, quarks, leptons, gauge bosons, symmetries, and fundamental interactions. Current research in high-energy physics.
Wave phenomena, oscillations, interference, diffraction, geometric optics, and modern optics applications. Laboratory experiments included.

Comprehensive software engineering course covering all phases of software development lifecycle including requirements gathering and analysis, system design using UML and design patterns, implementation best practices including coding standards and version control, comprehensive testing strategies covering unit testing, integration testing, system testing and acceptance testing, software maintenance and evolution, project management using both traditional waterfall and agile methodologies including Scrum and Kanban, software quality assurance, risk management, cost estimation, team dynamics and communication, software architecture patterns including microservices and event-driven architecture, DevOps practices including continuous integration and continuous deployment, containerization using Docker, orchestration with Kubernetes, monitoring and logging, security best practices, performance optimization, scalability considerations, database design and optimization, API design, documentation practices, code review processes, technical debt management, and emerging trends in software engineering. The course includes extensive hands-on projects simulating real-world software development scenarios, team-based assignments requiring collaboration and communication, individual coding challenges, comprehensive case studies of successful and failed software projects, guest lectures from industry professionals, and a capstone project involving designing and implementing a complete software system from requirements through deployment.
Intensive 8-week bootcamp covering frontend (React, HTML, CSS) and backend (Node.js, databases) web development. Project-based learning with daily coding challenges.
Introduction to quantum computing principles, qubits, quantum gates, and simple quantum algorithms. Designed for students without advanced physics background.
Mathematical foundations of cryptography including number theory and security protocols.
State-of-the-art NLP: transformers, BERT, GPT, attention mechanisms, transfer learning, and modern language model architectures. Research-oriented course.
Process management, memory management, file systems, concurrency, synchronization, and system calls. Hands-on kernel programming projects.
Rigorous probability theory: random variables, probability distributions, expectation, conditional probability, law of large numbers, and central limit theorem.
Image processing, feature detection, object recognition, deep learning for vision, convolutional neural networks, and vision transformers.
